standard: GDD rework v2 · 80+ researched scenarios · scorecard-passed
gating: Open (adult, comprehensive, ungated) · educational, NOT legal advice
note: Adult rights: POSH/harassment, consent law, work/tenancy/cyber rights (UNESCO 2.2, 4.3, 3.3). New v2 build, the College node that closes the chapter by turning the rights work of Justice League (g35) into the adult arenas a young adult now enters: the workplace and internships, harassment and POSH, renting a room, consumer and cyber rights, and the law in relationships. Six modes: rights at work, harassment & POSH, renting & consumer, cyber & data, claim it (UN&RE: 'you can't fight the system' -> you can; redress & free legal aid), tools/help. Empowering and practical: knowing your rights, and the routes to claim them, is one of the strongest protections an adult has. Educational, NOT legal advice; all law content flagged for expert review, localisation and currency. India: POSH Act 2013 and Internal Committees (10+ employees, complaint within 3 months, covers interns), basic labour/internship and tenancy/deposit norms, Consumer Protection Act 2019, cyber rights and DPDP, redress via Internal Committees, police/FIR and free legal aid (NALSA, 15100); helplines 181, 1091, 112, 1930, 1098. Builds on g35 (Justice League); pairs with g50; precedes the c6 capstone. Plain, usable for working youth (Meena, Farhan's cohort).

evidenceBase: Adults hold real rights at work and in a rented home, even when junior: a contract or offer should state pay, hours and role, wages must be paid for work done, and interns and contract workers have protections too, so unpaid 'internships' doing real work, or wages withheld, are not okay. Sexual harassment at work or college is illegal and has formal redress under India's POSH Act 2013: every workplace with 10 or more employees (and colleges) must have an Internal Committee, a complaint can be filed within three months (extendable), the process is confidential, and the Act covers regular, temporary, contract, part-time and intern women; harassment is never the price of a job (India Code, POSH Act 2013; labour law)

Tenancy, consumer and cyber rights protect young adults in plain terms: a rent agreement protects both sides and deposits are returnable minus genuine, documented damages; consumer law (the Consumer Protection Act 2019) gives rights to refund or replacement for defective goods and a route to complain; and online fraud, harassment, blackmail and non-consensual intimate images can be reported at the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal cybercrime.gov.in or helpline 1930, with personal data protected under the DPDP Act. Image-based abuse is a crime and the fault of the perpetrator, never the victim (Consumer Protection Act 2019; IT/cyber law; DPDP Act)

Redress is reachable, not just for the rich or connected: 'you can't fight the system' is false, because for a serious (cognizable) offence registering an FIR is mandatory and a Zero FIR can be filed at any station, and free legal aid is available through the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) and the Legal Services Authorities for anyone who can't afford a lawyer (helpline 15100). This is educational, not legal advice, with all law flagged for expert review, localisation and currency, and live harassment or abuse routed to the right committee and helplines (181, 1091, 112, 1930, 1098); knowing the route is half the protection (Lalita Kumari / FIR; NALSA / Article 39A free legal aid)
